solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Rap over the knuckles? This could make gent ill (7-3)

blocks.note: the surface reading: a reprimand, figuratively a smack on the hand
the setter's reading: the answer, taken as a recipe, is a word plus an instruction that jumbles it into these seven letters

annotation.surface: A scolding so harsh it leaves a gentleman feeling unwell.
annotation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the recipe. Take TELLING, apply OFF as an anagram signal, and you get GENT ILL. The question mark flags the joke.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative smack on the hand is the everyday British phrase for a scolding.

entries.clue: Can opener in your mini (4)

indicatorNotes.opener: the opener of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether there is a can opener in your little car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can opener' looks like one kitchen tool; split it so 'Can' is TIN and 'opener' works on 'your'. A Mini is a small British car, which is the surface image.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: mini is used as an adjective for anything very small.

entries.clue: Places old cat gets surrounded by big ones (9)

indicatorNotes.gets surrounded by: the preceding letters are placed inside what follows

blocks.note: lions are big cats, 'ones' standing for cats
O is a standard abbreviation for old

annotation.surface: An elderly house cat finds itself among lions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Big ones' only makes sense by borrowing the word before it: 'ones' stands in for cats, so the clue gets double duty from a single noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both name spots or sites where something is found.

entries.clue: Children in the US signed up (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits inside the words that follow
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, reading upwards turns the letters round

annotation.surface: Kids in America have been enrolled in something.
annotation.walkthrough: The word is used formally and legally for a person's descendants, as in 'died without issue'.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal and formal sense: a person's direct descendants, as in wills and titles.

entries.clue: Judged client in audition (7)

indicatorNotes.in audition: audition is hearing, so the word is to be heard, not read

blocks.note: a guest is a hotel's client; said out loud it matches a past tense meaning estimated

annotation.surface: A casting director assessed a customer who turned up to audition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Audition' pretends to be a stage tryout; here it means the act of hearing.
annotation.definitionFit: In the sense of estimating: forming an opinion without full knowledge.

entries.clue: Discovered half of shed is built (7)

indicatorNotes.half of: keep only half of the word's letters

annotation.surface: Someone found out a garden shed is only half built.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half of' does not say which half; only ED fits.
annotation.definitionFit: To found a building is to lay its base, so to establish or put it up.

entries.clue: Prevent beer bellies returning (4)

indicatorNotes.returning: going back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a pot, or pot belly, is a paunch

annotation.surface: A resolution to stop beer guts coming back.
annotation.walkthrough: A beer belly is also called a pot belly, or just a pot.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to halt something before it can happen.

entries.clue: Test result finally upset Den (5)

indicatorNotes.finally: the last letter of the word before it
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, knocked over so it reads upwards

blocks.note: a lair is an animal's den

annotation.surface: A test came back and finally upset someone called Den.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Den' looks like a name, as with Den Watts of the British soap EastEnders; its capital hides a plain noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an experiment to see how something performs.

entries.clue: Nine thumps? Barbaric chastisement (10)

indicatorNotes.Barbaric: savage, so the letters are roughly mangled

annotation.surface: Nine blows as a penalty: a brutal beating.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is itself a punishment, which is why the anagram hides so well.
annotation.definitionFit: Chastisement is the formal word for a penalty inflicted for wrongdoing.

entries.clue: I caught husband coated in adhesive mixture (8)

indicatorNotes.coated in: the letters are covered on both sides by the next word

blocks.note: c = caught, the cricket scorecard abbreviation

annotation.surface: Someone confesses they caught their husband covered in glue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught' and 'husband' read as a domestic confession; both are single-letter abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: A work blending borrowed styles is a medley, so a mixture.

entries.clue: Prison’s thieves (5)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Prison's' is read as 'prison is'; 'thieves' is the verb, as in 'he thieves'

blocks.note: British slang for a jail or police station, with 's = is
read as a verb: British slang for steals

annotation.surface: A prison full of thieves.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses are British slang: the nick is prison (also a police station) and to nick is to steal. 'Thieves' must be read as a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are British slang: a jail or police cell, and the verb to steal.

entries.clue: Cautioned about training (9)

indicatorNotes.about: turned around, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone was warned about their training.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' reads like 'concerning'; here it tells you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: schooling, the training of the mind.

entries.clue: Beginning to shed a bit of hair? Edward’s worried (8)

indicatorNotes.Beginning to: the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: a tress is a lock of hair
Ed is the short form of the name Edward

annotation.surface: Edward is anxious because his hair is starting to fall out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to shed' reads as a phrase about balding; it only asks for S. The 's is 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: under mental strain, anxious.

entries.clue: Cheers the Parisian’s stories (5)

blocks.note: ta is British informal for thanks, like 'cheers'

annotation.surface: A toast to a Frenchman's anecdotes.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain both 'cheers' and 'ta' mean thank you. A Parisian word for 'the' is French.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: narratives, often invented ones.

entries.clue: Be aware of rise in value (10)

blocks.note: to recognise or understand a point
what an asset does as its price climbs

annotation.surface: Advice to notice when an investment is going up.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses share a root but are used in quite different worlds: understanding and finance.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: to recognise the worth of something, and for an asset to gain in price.

entries.clue: Go for scheme I’d oddly dismissed (7)

indicatorNotes.oddly dismissed: the odd-numbered letters are thrown out, keeping the even ones

annotation.surface: Someone backs a plan even though their own part in it was oddly thrown out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go for' looks like a single phrase meaning choose; the definition is just 'Go', and 'for' is PRO.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to move forward or carry on.

entries.clue: Being cross with one pop star after end of performance (8)

indicatorNotes.end of: the last letter of the next word
indicatorNotes.after: the pieces before it come after this letter

annotation.surface: A pop star is annoyed once the show is over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' wants to mean angry, but it is the letter X.
annotation.definitionFit: As a participle, being means having existence now, as in 'for the time being'.

entries.clue: Editor rejected request for lecture (7)

indicatorNotes.rejected: thrown back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a claim is a demand or request

annotation.surface: An editor turned down a request to give a talk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' reads as refused; it only turns ED round.
annotation.definitionFit: To speak in a loud, formal, rhetorical way, as a lecturer might.

entries.clue: Confident vet raises cuckoo (9)

indicatorNotes.cuckoo: crazy, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: A self-assured vet rears a cuckoo chick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' poses as the bird being raised; it means mad and mixes up the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: self-assured and forceful in stating views.

entries.clue: Regretting keeping small hotel running (7)

blocks.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone regrets running a tiny hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Running' tempts as 'managing' the hotel; it is the definition, meaning hurrying.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: hurrying, moving at speed.

entries.clue: Wave perhaps gets moving on river (7)

blocks.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

annotation.surface: A surfer's wave gets moving along a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks a wave as one example of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: waving a hand is one of many meaningful bodily movements.

entries.clue: Essentially political motive for crime (7)

indicatorNotes.Essentially: at its essence, the heart of the word

annotation.surface: The motive behind the crime was basically political.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' reads as 'basically'; it takes the central letter of a nine-letter word.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: betraying one's country is one specific offence.

entries.clue: Teacher initially goes on about student trips (7)

indicatorNotes.initially: the first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: to rave is to go on enthusiastically
L = learner, as on British learner-driver plates

annotation.surface: A teacher starts talking at length about a school trip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Goes on' is two words for one piece, and 'about' wraps it round the student.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: journeys, as in a person's time abroad.

entries.clue: The chap’s enthralled by court case (5)

indicatorNotes.enthralled by: held captive inside the next piece

blocks.note: ct = court, as in street addresses

annotation.surface: A man is gripped by a court case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court case' reads as a lawsuit; split it so 'case' is a box.
annotation.definitionFit: A large strong box for storing things, the container sense of case.

entries.clue: The King’s constrained by tunnel vision (5)

indicatorNotes.constrained by: held inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A monarch is hampered by a narrow outlook.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The King' suggests a crowned monarch (R or K); it is a singer's nickname. The 's is 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Presley's nickname was the King of Rock and Roll.

entries.clue: Typical celebrity – eating and drinking, primarily (8)

indicatorNotes.primarily: first letter of the word before it

annotation.surface: The usual celebrity lifestyle, mostly food and drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eating and drinking' looks like a single pair; only 'eating' is an instruction, and 'and' is swallowed whole.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: normal, usual, what is expected.

entries.clue: Follow mother’s teaching (5)

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely

annotation.surface: Advice to obey your mother's instruction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mother's teaching' looks like one phrase; the 's is 'is', splitting wordplay from definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A fixed body of doctrine, the teaching of a church or party.

entries.clue: Festivity’s no good, regrettably (4)

blocks.note: a gala is a festivity; 's = is, giving GALA'S

annotation.surface: The party is no fun, sadly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No good' reads as a verdict on the party; it just strikes out G.
annotation.definitionFit: An interjection of sorrow, used where one would say regrettably.

entries.clue: Dancing at nude rave, wanting a thrilling experience (9)

indicatorNotes.wanting: lacking, so a letter is removed

annotation.surface: Dancing naked at a party, in search of a thrill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' pretends to mean desiring; it means lacking, and the 'a' after it is the letter lost.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an exciting or daring undertaking.

entries.clue: Gran? Not an awful cook (5)

annotation.surface: Protesting that grandma is not a terrible cook.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface defends Gran's cooking; 'cook' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: cooking under direct heat is one method of cooking.

entries.clue: Comfort guy scratching head (4)

blocks.note: to guy someone is to mock or tease them

annotation.surface: Soothing a man who is scratching his head in puzzlement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man; it is the old verb meaning to ridicule, which loses its head T.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, as a noun or verb: relief from pain or worry.

entries.clue: Wraps pens we damaged, but not with rags (10)

indicatorNotes.damaged: broken up, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone wraps broken pens but refuses to use old cloths.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rags' seems to be cleaning cloths; it is slang for low-grade papers. With the W gone, 10 letters remain.
annotation.definitionFit: Rag is disparaging slang for a low-quality paper.
